'''Margaret Cairns Etter''', known informally as '''Peggy Etter''' (12 September 1943 – 9 June 1992), was an American chemist who contributed to the development of solid state chemistry for crystalline organic compounds.<ref name="ChemMat_ob">{{cite journal |last1=Hollingsworth |first1=Mark D. |last2=Ward |first2=Michael D. |title=Margaret Cairns (Peggy) Etter 1943-1992 |journal=Chemistry of Materials |date=August 1994 |volume=6 |issue=8 |pages=1087–1089 |doi=10.1021/cm00044a001 }}</ref> She is known for her work characterizing and classifying contacts by [[hydrogen bond]]s in [[organic compound]]s. Her "enlightened imagination, innovative creativity, and unfailing enthusiasm"<ref name="CGD_spissue">{{cite web |last1=Bernstein |first1=Joel |title=Crystal Growth & Design: Margaret C. (Peggy) Etter Virtual Memorial Issue |url=https://pubs.acs.org/page/cgdefu/vi/16.html |website=pubs.acs.org |publisher=ACS |accessdate=13 September 2018}}</ref> is recognised as having a "transformative effect" in many areas of [[organic chemistry]].<ref name="CGD_WIC">{{cite journal |last1=Kahr |first1=Bart |title=Broader Impacts of Women in Crystallography |journal=Crystal Growth & Design |date=25 August 2015 |volume=15 |issue=10 |pages=4715–4730 |doi=10.1021/acs.cgd.5b00457|issn=1528-7483}}</ref>

== Education and career ==

Etter was born as Margaret Cairns in Greenville, a town in Delaware near Wilmington.<ref name="ChemMat_ob"/> Her father, [[Theodore L. Cairns]] ("Ted"), was a chemist by profession at DuPont.<ref name="CGD_ob">{{cite journal |last1=Bernstein |first1=Joel |title=Peggy Etter: A Personal Recollection |journal=Crystal Growth & Design |date=2 February 2016 |volume=16 |issue=3 |pages=1135–1143 |doi=10.1021/acs.cgd.5b01296|issn=1528-7483}}</ref> Etter attained her B.Sc. at the [[University of Pennsylvania]], spending a freshman semester at [[Cornell]] (where she met future collaborator Joel Bernstein in the Mugwuamp freshman orientation group<ref name="CGD_ob"/>), and completed a master's degree at the [[University of Delaware]] in 1971 with Harold Kwart.<ref name="ChemMat_ob"/> Her Ph.D. research was completed at the [[University of Minnesota]]<ref>{{cite book |last1=Etter |first1=Margaret Cairns |title=Solid-state Chemistry and Crystallography of Two Polymorphs of 1-methoxy-1, 2-benziodoxolin-3-one |date=1974 |publisher=Ph.D. Univ. of Minnesota |url=https://primo.lib.umn.edu/primo-explore/fulldisplay?docid=UMN_ALMA21425020660001701&context=L&vid=TWINCITIES&search_scope=mncat_discovery&tab=article_discovery&lang=en_US |ref=University of Minnesota Catalog (9940230860001701)}}</ref> as a [[National Science Foundation]] predoctoral fellow under the supervision of Jack Gougoutas. Her thesis and postdoctoral work focused on the study of the chemical and structural properties of polyvalent iodine compounds using [[X-ray diffraction]] and spectroscopic techniques.<ref name="ChemMat_ob"/> Her Ph. D work was published<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gougoutas |first1=Jack Zanos |last2=Chang |first2=Kuo H. |last3=Etter |first3=Margaret C. |title=Solid-state chemistry of organic polyvalent iodine compounds. VI. The crystal structure and topotactic hydrolysis of 3-oxo-3H-2,1-benzoxiodol-1-yl o-fluorobenzoate |journal=Journal of Solid State Chemistry |date=15 January 1976 |volume=16 |issue=3–4 |pages=283–291 |doi=10.1016/0022-4596(76)90043-8 |bibcode=1976JSSCh..16..283G |issn=0022-4596}}</ref> and still provides a model for how topotactic reactions should be studied.<ref name="CGD_ob"/>

After a brief stay as an assistant professor at [[Augsburg College]], Etter obtained employment in the Central Research Laboratories at the mile-square [[3M]] campus in [[Maplewood, Minnesota]], as a researcher.<ref name="CGD_ob"/> She collaborated with several research groups to study crystalline compounds and [[polymers]], including molecular salts based on two photographic dyes that formed no fewer than 14 [[Polymorphism (materials science)|polymorphs]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Etter |first1=Margaret C. |last2=Kress |first2=Ruth B. |last3=Bernstein |first3=Joel |last4=Cash |first4=Derek J. |title=Solid-state chemistry and structures of a new class of mixed dyes. Cyanine-oxonol |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |date=November 1984 |volume=106 |issue=23 |pages=6921–6927 |doi=10.1021/ja00335a009|issn=0002-7863}}</ref>

Due to the difficulties of maintaining a stable research program at 3M,<ref name="CGD_ob"/> Etter returned to the University of Minnesota first as a [[postdoctoral researcher]] in [[solid state NMR]] with Robert Bryant, and later as professor (from 1984) at the school of chemistry. For the rest of her career she devoted herself to the investigation of the properties of crystalline solids and hydrogen bonds. Her work influenced several areas of interest in the field of solid state organic chemistry, such as crystal growth, [[clathrate]] formation, [[phase transitions]], [[supramolecular chemistry]] and [[cocrystal|co-crystals]] (a term she essentially defined in the community<ref name="CGD_ob"/>).<ref name="ChemMat_ob"/> Much of her work was truly interdisciplinary. Etter's key contribution was the use of graph sets to analyze hydrogen bond patterns (rather than the more conventional analysis of individual bonds), a path against the prevailing attitude that hydrogen bonding in organic solids was too complicated to understand.<ref name="ChemMat_ob"/> The establishing of the "Etter Rules" was later reported in Accounts of Chemical Research "Encoding and Decoding Hydrogen Bond Patterns in Organic Compounds"<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Etter |first1=Margaret C. |title=Encoding and decoding hydrogen-bond patterns of organic compounds |journal=Accounts of Chemical Research |date=April 1990 |volume=23 |issue=4 |pages=120–126 |doi=10.1021/ar00172a005|issn=0001-4842}}</ref> which since has been cited more than 4,000 times.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://scholar.google.co.uk/scholar?cites=3595153990226750846&as_sdt=2005&sciodt=0,5&hl=en|title=List of citations to ''Encoding and decoding hydrogen-bond patterns of organic compounds'' by Margaret C. Etter|publisher=Google Scholar|accessdate=15 November 2018}}</ref><ref name="CGD_WIC"/> Such representation is widely used in structural chemistry and solid state chemistry for the description of organic compounds.<ref name="ChemMat_ob"/><ref name="ActaCryst_graph">{{cite journal |last1=Grell |first1=J. |last2=Bernstein |first2=J. |last3=Tinhofer |first3=G. |title=Graph-set analysis of hydrogen-bond patterns: some mathematical concepts |journal=Acta Crystallographica Section B |date=1 December 1999 |volume=55 |issue=6 |pages=1030–1043 |doi=10.1107/S0108768199007120 |pmid=10927445 |issn=0108-7681|doi-access= |bibcode=1999AcCrB..55.1030G }}</ref> The use of "Etter Rules"<ref name="ChemMat_ob"/> was reviewed (with further results incorporated) in Angewandte Chemie,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bernstein |first1=Joel |last2=Davis |first2=Raymond E. |last3=Shimoni |first3=Liat |last4=Chang |first4=Ning-Leh |title=Patterns in Hydrogen Bonding: Functionality and Graph Set Analysis in Crystals |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition in English |date=18 August 1995 |volume=34 |issue=15 |pages=1555–1573 |doi=10.1002/anie.199515551|issn=0570-0833}}</ref> and the approach was incorporated into the CSD software for automatic analysis of structures.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Motherwell |first1=W. D. Samuel |last2=Shields |first2=Gregory P. |last3=Allen |first3=Frank H. |title=Visualization and characterization of non-covalent networks in molecular crystals: automated assignment of graph-set descriptors for asymmetric molecules |journal=Acta Crystallographica Section B |date=1 December 1999 |volume=55 |issue=6 |pages=1044–1056 |doi=10.1107/S0108768199006497 |pmid=10927446 |bibcode=1999AcCrB..55.1044M |issn=0108-7681}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Motherwell |first1=W. D. Samuel |last2=Shields |first2=Gregory P. |last3=Allen |first3=Frank H. |title=Automated assignment of graph-set descriptors for crystallographically symmetric molecules |journal=Acta Crystallographica Section B |date=1 June 2000 |volume=56 |issue=3 |pages=466–473 |doi=10.1107/S0108768100001683 |pmid=10877355 |bibcode=2000AcCrB..56..466M |url=https://journals.iucr.org/b/issues/2000/03/00/ha0194/index.html|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In April 1991 Etter was diagnosed with stage IV kidney cancer, in the most productive phase of her career that she herself described as being "on a roll".<ref name="ChemMat_ob"/><ref name="CGD_ob"/> Her final appearance was on a tour of Israel to coincide with the [https://www.chemistry.org.il/ics/history/ Israel Chemical Society] Annual Meeting, when she visited the [[Weizmann Institute]] and the [[Technion]], places she had always wanted to visit due to the concentration of organic solid-state chemists.<ref name="CGD_ob"/> Additionally, during this visit she gave a plenary lecture on her research.<ref name="CGD_ob" /> Shortly after her return to the United States, Etter was placed in hospice care due to a rapid deterioration of her health. She died on June 9, 1992.<ref name="CGD_ob" />

== Awards and recognition ==

In 1979, Etter received the "Good Neighbor" award from the Minnesota radio station [[WCCO (AM)|WCCO]] for her contributions to the development of the school science program STEP at 3M.<ref name="ChemMat_ob"/> Her outreach work focused on improving the opportunities for women in science, lecturing on the subject to high school and college students, and serving as a role model for female undergraduate and graduate students.<ref name="CGD_ob"/> During her illness on [[Thanksgiving Day]] 1991, [[Minnesota Public Radio]] paid a special tribute to her.<ref name="ChemMat_ob"/>

Etter was recognized as an early pioneer in the Chemistry Department of the University of Minnesota due to the research she conducted related to "... the applications of solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, the design and properties of organic non-linear optical materials, and most significantly, in the understanding and utilization of hydrogen-bonding interactions in crystals." Her work was recognized with many international awards and fellowships through her career:<ref name="memlec">{{cite web |title=Margaret C. Etter Memorial Lecture in Materials Chemistry |url=https://chem.umn.edu/event-type/margaret-c-etter-memorial-lecture-materials-chemistry |website=Department of Chemistry}}</ref>
* Sloan Research Fellowship (1989)<ref>{{cite web |title=Past Fellows |url=https://sloan.org/past-fellows |website=sloan.org}}</ref>
* Bush Foundation Fellowship
* [[Iota Sigma Pi]] Award for Excellence in Chemistry 
* St. Paul Businessperson of the Year (1986) for her work with “Rochelle Crystal Corporation.”

In recognition of both her scientific achievements and her work as a mentor to students and novice scientists, the [[American Crystallographic Association]] launched two awards in honor of Peggy Etter: the Margaret C. Etter Early Career Award, given to scientists who have made important contributions early in their careers, and the Margaret C. Etter Student Lecturer Award, awarded to a selection of students for their oral presentations at the annual conference of the association.<ref>{{cite web|title=ACA Council News|url=https://www.amercrystalassn.org/assets/RefleXions/2003Spring.pdf|work=ACA Newsletter Spring 2003|page=6|publisher=American Crystallographic Association|accessdate=15 November 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=(IUCr) American Crystallographic Association awards |url=https://www.iucr.org/news/newsletter/volume-10/number-2/aca-awards |website=www.iucr.org |publisher=IUCr |accessdate=7 September 2018}}</ref>

In addition, the University of Minnesota holds an annual Etter Memorial Lecture<ref name="memlec" /> and hosts an endowed lectureship in solid state chemistry and materials science bearing her name.<ref name="ChemMat_ob" />
